auth.notes: Classic HealthManager uses a login API on the BHMCWebAPI host; the Pro app authenticates via its SSO hosts. Not mapped further — the device never contacts any cloud, so none of this is on the local-control path.

data_leaves_device: SpO2/pulse measurement history uploaded by the phone app, only when the user signs into an account
cloud.failure_mode: Nothing breaks on the device. The PO60 is phone-to-device over BLE only; the cloud exists solely as optional account/sync storage inside the companion apps (both of which also work in guest/local mode). Beurer GmbH is alive and the Pro app is actively maintained, so there is no shutdown risk today — and even a total cloud shutdown would leave measurement, storage and sync to any BLE client fully functional.
hosts: https://sync.connect-beurer.com/BHMCWebAPI/ (legacy HealthManager: login, user management, measurement sync up/down)
cloud.notes: Device imagery for the Pro app is served from an Azure CDN (beur-hm-api-cdn-endpoint-prod / -produs .azureedge.net) — cosmetic only.
cloud.vendor_service: beurer HealthManager / HealthManager Pro cloud (optional account sync from the phone app)

device.name: Beurer PO60 Pulse Oximeter
device.notes:
Bluetooth Smart (BLE 4.0) fingertip pulse oximeter by Beurer (Ulm, Germany — company founded 1919, alive and shipping; the Pro app was still updated as of v1.22.0, Aug 2026). Measures SpO2 and pulse rate, stores up to 100 measurement sessions on-device, color OLED display. Advertises as `PO60` (confirmed in both apps' scan filters).
The device speaks ONE custom GATT service (FF12 on the standard 0000xxxx-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb base) with a write characteristic (FF01) for commands and a notify characteristic (FF02) for acks and history data. It does NOT implement the standard BLE Pulse Oximeter profile (0x1822 PLX) — per both apps; no on-air confirmation yet.
The interaction model is history sync, not live streaming: the app bonds (standard BLE passkey, 6-digit PIN from the device manual), enables notifications, sets the clock, then pages the stored-session log with a 3-command protocol until an end-of-transfer record arrives, and disconnects. No command for streaming an in-progress measurement was found in either app — whether the hardware can do that at all is unknown.
OEM is unidentified. The BLE stack is the same "ilink" SDK (com.ilink.bleapi) that drives the whole Beurer/Sanitas medical line (BF scales, BM blood-pressure monitors, GL glucose, AS activity sensors, FT thermometers), so the PO60 firmware almost certainly comes from Beurer's usual Chinese ODM; no rebranded sibling is known.
FCC ID: not found — the US manual carries only a generic Part 15 statement and no FCC ID string; needs a label photo or fccid.io visual search.
No firmware update path exists: neither app contains any DFU/OTA code for the PO60 (the only FirmwareRevisionString reads in the codebase are on scales), and no firmware URLs were found.

issued_to_client: Nothing beyond the BLE bond itself; there are no per-device application credentials
stored_on_device: BLE bond (link-layer keys) per paired phone
Measurement history (up to 100 sessions) — health data, at rest unencrypted, readable by any bonded client

factory_reset.effect: Not established. The device holds up to 100 measurement records plus BLE bonding state, but no reset procedure was found in either companion app or in the US manual text examined. Do not guess one.

ble.pin_source: 6-digit passkey printed in the device manual (app prompts for it as a pairing key)

methods.description: Scan for `PO60`, connect, bond with the 6-digit passkey from the device manual, enable notifications on FF02, sync the clock, then page the measurement log.

steps.action: Power on the PO60 and scan for the exact local name `PO60`.
Connect and complete BLE passkey bonding (6-digit PIN from the manual).
steps.expect: Bonded link; GATT service FF12 with characteristics FF01 (write) and FF02 (notify).

steps.action: Enable notifications on FF02 (write the CCC descriptor).
Set the device clock (command 0x83 on FF01; both apps do this immediately after bonding).
Read storage info (90 05 15), then page the log with 99 00 19 / 99 01 1A until an E9 4x end-of-transfer record arrives.

setup.notes: Nothing to provision — no network, no account. The one gate is BLE bonding: the PO60 appears in the apps' pairing-key device list, i.e. pairing is standard BLE passkey entry with the 6-digit PIN printed in the device manual. Whether some firmware revisions accept Just-Works instead, and whether an unbonded client can already write the time-set command, is unknown (needs hardware). Confidence medium: read from both companion apps, not replayed here.

rejoin.notes: Rebinding to a new phone is ordinary BLE bonding: remove the old bond in the previous phone's OS Bluetooth settings if the device refuses to pair, then bond again with the manual PIN. Measurement history survives on the device.

testing.notes: No hardware on the bench. All protocol facts were recovered by static analysis of the classic HealthManager and HealthManager Pro apps and agree between the two; a third-party bleak script (Shreyan1, see sources) reports working against a real PO60 with the same UUIDs and command bytes — that supports per-fact `reported`, not this flag.

helpful_urls.description: Third-party bleak (Python) script that polls a real PO60 with the same FF01/FF02 UUIDs and the 90 05 15 / 99 00 19 command bytes documented here — the closest thing to a working reference client, and the right starting point for a Home Assistant polling script.

covers: Full stored-measurement sync: per-session start/end time plus SpO2 and pulse-rate min/max/avg, paged over FF02 notifications
not_covered: Live/streaming SpO2 during a reading — no such command exists in either app; unknown whether the hardware supports it at all
Firmware update — no OTA/DFU path exists in either app and no firmware image is public
Deleting records from the device — no such command was found
local_access.summary: Fully local by design: the only radio is BLE, and the complete documented function set (clock sync + full measurement-history pull) is reachable with the three commands in this spec from any BLE host.

framing.byte_order: big (all fields are single bytes; the year field is year-2000)
framing.checksum: Low-7-bit additive: CKS = (sum of preceding frame bytes) & 0x7F for the 0x83 time-set command; the 0x99 page command uses (page - 103) & 0x7F. No CRC, no length prefix, no encryption.
framing.notes: Notification path reassembly: measurement data arrives as 20-byte chunks on FF02; concatenate and slice into 24-byte records starting at each 0xE9 header. Bytes 15, 16 and 23 of the record are unused/unknown.

remaining_unknowns: Whether the PO60 also exposes standard PLX (0x1822) or a battery service alongside FF12 (the app code says no; confirm on-air)
Exact format/length of the storage-info response to 90 05 15
Page-size semantics of the 0x99 command (12 records/page inferred, not confirmed)
Whether the bonding passkey is fixed per device (printed in manual) or Just-Works on some firmware revisions
Whether an unbonded client can already write the time-set command (decides whether third-party clients need the PIN at all)
FCC ID (absent from the US manual; needs a device-label photo)

session_flow.description:
Post-connect sequence, as both apps drive it: 1. Bond (BLE passkey, PIN from manual) and enable notifications on FF02. 2. Write set_datetime (0x83 ...) to FF01; expect ack F3 00 on FF02. 3. Write read_storage_info (90 05 15); the FF02 response carries the
   stored-record count (exact response layout still unpinned).
4. Write get_measurements_page START (99 00 19); records stream on FF02
   as 20-byte chunks.
5. Every 12 records, write NEXT (99 01 1A) to page onward (page size 12
   is inferred from the classic app's record-index constant, not
   hardware-confirmed).
6. Stop at the end-of-transfer record (header E9, byte 1 high nibble
   0x4). The app disconnects about 3 s later.
session_flow.verification_note: Read from both companion apps; corroborated by a third-party hardware-tested bleak script; not replayed by this project.

get_measurements_page.description: Request a page of the stored-measurement log on FF02. pp = 0x00 starts the transfer, pp = 0x01 fetches the next page (the app pages every 12 records until the E9 4x end-of-transfer record). Checksum for this command is (pp - 103) & 0x7F, giving the observed on-the-wire bytes 99 00 19 and 99 01 1A.

read_storage_info.description: Query the number of stored measurement records; the device answers on FF02

set_datetime.description: Set the device clock. CKS = (sum of bytes 0..7) & 0x7F. Device acks on FF02 with F3 00. The legacy app wrote placeholder 05 05 05 in the seconds/pad positions; HealthManager Pro sends real seconds — send real time.

checksum.description: (0x83 + year + month + day + hour + minute + second + 0x00 + 0x00) & 0x7F. NOT expressible as the schema's `auto: checksum` (that is sum mod 256); compute it per this rule.

characteristics.name: Command (write)
characteristics.notes: All commands are written here. Checksum rule (both apps): low-7-bit additive — CKS = (sum of the preceding bytes) & 0x7F, except the 0x99 page command, whose last byte is (pp - 103) & 0x7F. The concrete command bytes below match the third-party hardware-tested bleak script (Shreyan1).

format.name: header
format.notes: Every record starts 0xE9. NOTE: this format describes the reassembled 24-byte record, NOT a single notification value — notifications arrive as 20-byte chunks and must be concatenated before slicing.

format.name: record_index
format.notes: Low nibble = packet/record index. High nibble 0x4 marks end-of-transfer (no more pages; client may disconnect).

format.name: end_year
format.notes: Measurement end time, same layout as start.

format.name: pr_escape_flags
format.notes: Bit 2 -> add 128 to PR max, bit 3 -> add 128 to PR min, bit 4 -> add 128 to PR avg. Escape for pulse values that exceed the 7-bit field range.

format.name: pr_max
format.notes: Add 128 when bit 2 of pr_escape_flags is set.

format.name: pr_min
format.notes: Add 128 when bit 3 of pr_escape_flags is set.

format.name: pr_avg
format.notes: Add 128 when bit 4 of pr_escape_flags is set.

characteristics.name: Response / measurement data (notify)
characteristics.notes:
Ack and data channel. Known frame types (app-parsed): - Time-set ack: F3 00. - Storage-info response to 90 05 15: carries the stored-record
  count; exact length/offset of the count byte is NOT yet pinned
  down (open question).
- Measurement records: stream as 20-byte notification chunks; the
  client reassembles and slices 24-byte records (see `format` for
  the record layout). A record whose byte 1 has high nibble 0x4
  marks end-of-transfer; the app disconnects about 3 s later.
All numeric fields are plain 7-bit integers (mask 0x7F); pulse-rate values >= 128 escape via the flag byte at offset 14 (bit 2 -> +128 to PR max, bit 3 -> PR min, bit 4 -> PR avg).

services.name: Beurer Pulse Oximeter Service
services.notes: The only application service. 16-bit alias FF12 on the standard BLE base UUID. The device does NOT expose the SIG Pulse Oximeter profile (0x1822 PLX) per both apps; whether a battery service or PLX shows up alongside FF12 on-air is an open question. No encryption anywhere in the protocol — plain BLE bonding is the only protection, and all multi-byte values are plain 7-bit-masked integers.

sources.description: Static analysis of the beurer HealthManager Pro app (2026-08) — the currently maintained companion. Kotlin, obfuscated, built on RxAndroidBle; its PO60 sync repository is the cross-check for the record layout and command bytes.
sources.obtained_via: third-party APK mirror, 2026-08 (a v1.17.2 partial download was discarded; v1.17.1 is complete)

sources.description: Static analysis of the classic beurer HealthManager app (2026-08) — the older, essentially unobfuscated companion. Its shared BLE API and pulse-oximeter utilities are where the record layout, the supported service map and the command bytes were read first, then cross-checked against the Pro app.
Independent corroboration: bleak script using FF01/FF02, the 90 05 15 and 99 00 19 commands, and E9-framed record parsing — matches the static analysis. Reported working against real hardware.

Beurer PO60 US manual (PDF), sha256 f2c3d26895185f31dace54a52c952e8520944ebd50fd89c4dae4d73bc20f31a2. Source of the 6-digit pairing PIN and the 100-session storage claim; contains only a generic FCC Part 15 statement — no FCC ID.

beurer HealthCoach, the app named in the US manual, is pulled from stores and was not examined. Judged obsolete: same underlying BLE stack, superseded by HealthManager/Pro — no protocol fact here depends on it.
